stem.en: You shout near a hard wall. In one place the reflection reaches you 0.06 s after your shout. In another place it reaches you 1.2 s after your shout. Where do you hear the reflection as a separate sound?

text.en: In both places, because both walls are hard.
Only where it takes 1.2 s, because two sounds must be at least 0.1 s apart to be heard separately.
Only where it takes 0.06 s, because a nearer wall gives a stronger reflection.
In neither place, because a reflection always mixes with the shout.

explanation.en: You hear two sounds separately only if they reach you at least 0.1 s apart. A reflection 0.06 s after the shout mixes with it. A reflection 1.2 s later is heard separately: it is an echo.

hints.en: What is the shortest gap at which you hear two separate sounds?
Compare 0.06 s and 1.2 s with 0.1 s.
